answer: Agents must publish collateral to an append-only registry before earning reputation. Each new identity locks funds, and withdrawals wait through a challenge period in which peers can submit signed evidence that the same controller operates several accounts; a successful challenge slashes the linked collateral and redistributes it to reporters. Splitting one agent into a hundred aliases therefore multiplies the capital tied up and the chance of losing it, rather than creating free influence. Ivory, shale, or vertex may be an agent’s name, but none exempts it from the same bond and audit.
